cards.title: Vary Sentence Length for Rhythm
cards.summary: Alternate short, medium and long sentences to make copy flow and pull readers through.
cards.use_when: Editing store newsletters, landing pages or product descriptions that read flat or monotonous.

cards.title: The 'Letter from the CEO' Sales Page Pattern
cards.summary: A first-person letter from the founder using simple language can serve as an effective sales page format.
cards.use_when: Building or testing the top-of-page copy for a product landing page, especially for a subscription or considered purchase.

cards.title: The CEO Story That Earns Free Distribution
cards.summary: Stories with an outrage or 'WTF' emotional hook can generate organic pickup and be amplified by the subject.
cards.use_when: Sourcing or writing brand editorial content where you want the subject or third party to share or amplify it.

cards.title: Comedy Techniques for Attention and Persuasion
cards.summary: Study comedians' timing, tension and self-deprecation for principles you can apply to brand storytelling and crisis response.
cards.use_when: Writing brand content, apology statements or acquisition creative where you need to hold attention and win the audience's trust.

cards.title: Find Untapped Content in Engineering/Tech Blog Posts
cards.summary: Detailed, obsessive blog posts from non-marketing authors often contain distinctive content angles.
cards.use_when: Sourcing content ideas or building brand-voice posts when your category's conventional marketing content is saturated.

cards.title: 'You Pushed Out': The Personal Monopoly Principle
cards.summary: Content that reflects your genuine interests and opinions attracts a loyal audience no competitor can replicate.
cards.use_when: Defining your store's content voice and deciding which topics the brand should own in its category.

cards.title: Copywork as Structured Practice for Better Copy
cards.summary: Retyping well-crafted passages by hand is a repeatable practice method for improving writing style.
cards.use_when: Training yourself or a content team on copy style, especially before producing a batch of store content or ad copy.

cards.title: AI Writes Slop Because It Doesn't Know Which Commodity Ideas You Agree With
cards.summary: Commodity content has value, and the differentiator is not a unique idea but which side of each settled debate your identity sits on, which AI cannot infer.
cards.use_when: Writing or briefing product-description and blog copy for a store, and AI output reads generic or off-brand and you're tempted to re-prompt rather than supply the missing perspective.

cards.title: Write From 'I', Not 'You', to Escape Commodity Copy
cards.summary: Copy that addresses the reader with 'you should' defaults to generic advice; copy written from 'I think / I did' produces personality content that differentiates.
cards.use_when: Drafting product descriptions, founder notes, or landing page copy and the paragraph reads like generic category advice that any store could publish.

cards.title: AI Should Repeat You, Not Write For You
cards.summary: AI's leverage is in recombining your approved language into new mixes, not in generating net-new thinking from the same public dataset every competitor uses.
cards.use_when: Setting up a content production workflow for a store — delegating blog, email, or social output to AI and deciding which parts a human must do first.

cards.title: Value Is Relative to Where Your Audience Is
cards.summary: Content value depends on the reader's stage, not the writer's, so advanced operators must deliberately decide whether to serve beginners with commodity content or serve peers with original thinking.
cards.use_when: Choosing what to publish for a store's blog or email list and deciding whether to write beginner 'how to choose' content or advanced, opinionated content for experienced customers.

cards.title: Build the 'Unmade Data Set' From Your Own Stories
cards.summary: Since every competitor trains on the same public corpus, your proprietary history — mistakes, specific lived details, your path — is the only data no one else has.
cards.use_when: Filling out a brand/about page, a founder newsletter, or a retention email series and looking for content that differentiates rather than repeats category knowledge.

cards.title: Personality Outperforms Credibility in Content
cards.summary: The source argues less-credentialed creators with strong personality content generally get more distribution than highly credentialed people producing flat commodity content.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much founder personality to expose versus how much 'expert' positioning to project on a store's about page, newsletter or founder-led social channel.

cards.title: Timely vs Timeless Content: Set Expectations Before You Publish
cards.summary: Every piece of content sits on a timely–timeless spectrum; timely content gives high 24-hour value and near-zero long-term value, and the reverse for timeless, so match expectations to the type.
cards.use_when: Planning a store's content calendar — deciding which launches, memes, or promotions to make and which should be evergreen pieces you re-use for years.

cards.title: Volume and Topic Concentration Create Association (Ownership Is Just Association)
cards.summary: You don't own words, ideas or phrases — you own the audience's association between a topic and you, and the simplest way to build it is to publish about a narrow set of topics repeatedly.
cards.use_when: Choosing what a store's content program should be known for, and deciding whether to write broadly or concentrate on a narrow set of positions to drive association with the category.

cards.title: Voice Is Built From Identifiable Variables, Not Magic
cards.summary: Voice is a bundle of word choice, sentence length/structure and perspective-taking that can be identified and edited rather than treated as untouchable mystique.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an AI-drafted product page, email or landing page that reads generic, and fixing it by editing the one variable that's off instead of discarding the whole draft.

cards.title: Write First to Discover Your Voice — Don't Wait For It
cards.summary: The source's position is that most people who say they don't like their voice are actually afraid to publish, and voice is discovered only by writing and publishing.
cards.use_when: Finding excuses to delay starting or delegating a store's content program, or when a founder says they have no voice and considers AI-generated copy a shortcut.

cards.title: Point of View Is the Moat — for a Product and a Content Program
cards.summary: SaaS and products with a specific method beat commodity feature sets because copying the output forces competitors to chase the methodology with a permanent lag.
cards.use_when: Positioning a store's product, subscription or membership, or writing the category positioning that explains why your way of doing the customer's job is different.

cards.title: Use Short/Medium/Long-Term Value to Choose What to Publish
cards.summary: Ask before creating what the short-, medium- and long-term value is; the same question applied to the store's 20-minute post and its two-week essay produces very different additive contributions to the content library.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend content production time for a store — which single blog post, guide, or campaign gets the two-week investment versus the twenty-minute one.

cards.title: What to Skip When Following This Framework
cards.summary: This material's useful core is the writing/publishing/ownership framework; tangential show content — sponsor reads, personal banter, agency plugs — is not part of it.
cards.use_when: Reviewing or applying the framework to decide what actually belongs in a store's content or writing-forward practice.

cards.title: Build a Company Brain as the Content Supply Chain
cards.summary: Treat a library of original long-form thinking as a compounding asset that feeds all downstream content, not a one-off piece of marketing.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to structure your store's content operation and where to invest the first content dollar before scaling volume.

cards.title: Use a Minimum Volume Floor to Test Content
cards.summary: Pick an output floor high enough that content gets a fair experiment, then build the system to hit it before optimizing timing or virality.
cards.use_when: Setting your store's weekly content cadence and deciding how many assets to publish before judging what works.

cards.title: Get Out of Your Own Way and Publish
cards.summary: Fear of sharing a 'commodity' perspective keeps sellers from publishing; most common ideas are not risky and the real value is discovering your voice through output.
cards.use_when: Stalling on publishing store content, founder POV, or category education because the idea feels too obvious or exposing.

cards.title: Build a Personal Language Model for Idea Supply
cards.summary: The volume floor only works if you have a structured source of ideas — a 'digital brain' or personal language model — feeding it.
cards.use_when: Scaling from occasional posts to a consistent content cadence and running out of things to say about your products or category.

cards.title: Treat Content as Data You Own and License
cards.summary: Language, writing and content libraries are data assets; their value depends on whether you have the infrastructure to mine and leverage them.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to buy, license, or commission content assets (writer catalogs, data sets) to fuel your store's marketing.

cards.title: Fund a Deep Thinker Over Promotional Output
cards.summary: The source's strongest opinion: the best marketing spend is hiring a thoughtful writer to produce original long-form thinking, not more promotional content.
cards.use_when: Allocating content budget or hiring for content and deciding whether to prioritize promotional copy or original category thinking.

cards.title: Separate Infrastructure From Idea Input
cards.summary: Posting volume is infrastructure; the harder question is the quality of input flowing into it — treat them as two distinct decisions.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why store content isn't working — is it cadence/distribution or is it the underlying ideas?

cards.title: Let Robots Repeat, Humans Originate
cards.summary: Assign AI the repeating/remixing work and keep humans on original thinking — this division is the source's core division of labor.
cards.use_when: Designing how much of your store's content production to automate versus keep human-authored.

cards.title: Prioritize Library Over Virality Tactics
cards.summary: The source dismisses tactical virality chasing in favor of a valuable content library pulled from repeatedly over time.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend limited content effort — micro-optimization versus building a reusable library for your store.

cards.title: Expect Media Components in Brand Strategy
cards.summary: The source observes large companies building media arms; for ecommerce this maps to owning category narrative, not just posting.
cards.use_when: Setting a long-term content direction for your brand and deciding whether to invest in owned media rather than relying on ad spend.

cards.title: Assess Content Assets by Leverage, Not Intrinsic Value
cards.summary: The source argues a content asset's value is determined by how well you can leverage it, not by what it is.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether to buy, license or commission content (writer catalogs, creator libraries, data sets) for your store.

cards.title: Story-First Creative Replaces Hook-Body-CTA
cards.summary: The source argues the old Hook-Body-CTA creative formula should be replaced with Frame Swipe -> Create a Story -> Scale.
cards.use_when: Planning organic content or paid social creative for a store's product, and deciding whether a script should lead with the product claim or with a narrative.

cards.title: Use Neural Coupling to Choose Story Over Specs
cards.summary: Stories activate sensory and emotional brain regions that facts do not, making narrative creative more memorable and visceral than feature lists.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to present product benefits on a landing page, PDP, or social ad when you are tempted to lead with specifications.

cards.title: Map Emotional Triggers Before Writing the Story
cards.summary: Ask which core emotion your product can activate — curiosity, moral outrage, belonging, confusion, visual shock — then build the narrative around it.
cards.use_when: Choosing a narrative angle for a product launch or evergreen creative, or briefing a creator on what feeling the video should produce.

cards.title: Mine Hidden Narratives With Founder Questions
cards.summary: A set of prompting questions surfaces the counterintuitive, controversial, and heartfelt stories a store already owns but has never told.
cards.use_when: Running out of creative angles for organic posts or paid ads and needing fresh product stories that are not feature lists.

cards.title: Turn Your Business History Into a Carousel in 30 Minutes
cards.summary: A fast exercise converts a founder's timeline, including failures, into a story-driven carousel post or reel script.
cards.use_when: A store owner needs a postable story asset today and has no creator or editor lined up.

cards.title: Frame Swipe Out-of-Niche Creatives
cards.summary: A structured teardown grid lets you ethically lift the format of a viral video from another niche and apply it to your product.
cards.use_when: Creating a new ad or organic creative format for a store and needing a proven structure without copying competitors' exact content.

cards.title: Open a Loop in the First Sentence Instead of a Hook
cards.summary: The Zeigarnik effect means viewers remember unresolved questions, so open curiosity early and deliberately delay closing it.
cards.use_when: Writing the opening line of a video or ad script and deciding how quickly to reveal the product answer.

cards.title: Exaggerate Language to Earn Algorithm Attention
cards.summary: Replacing corporate, hedged descriptions with deliberately strong language changes how the content is received and prioritized.
cards.use_when: Editing an ad script or social caption that reads flat and factual, and you need more stopping power.

cards.title: Diagnose the Founder Constraint Behind a Sales Plateau
cards.summary: When sales drop while the founder still films alone, the cause is often capped content volume rather than product or market failure.
cards.use_when: A store's revenue is flat or declining while a founder still personally creates most content and posts roughly once a day.

cards.title: Prefer Scalable Formats Over One-Off Founder Stories
cards.summary: Formats repeatable by a team compound output; a single founder story or a cooking/travel format cannot be produced at volume.
cards.use_when: Choosing which content format to build a production system around for a store's organic channel.

cards.title: Build a Creator Bench, Not a Corporate Social Hire
cards.summary: Hire people with proven views and native platform instincts, centralize all footage in a shared drive, and use overseas editors on performance incentives.
cards.use_when: Removing the founder as the content bottleneck by staffing up organic and paid creative production for a store.

cards.title: Life-Extend a Winning Viral Asset Across Formats and Accounts
cards.summary: Multiply the return on one proven story by reformatting it, swapping hooks, and reposting across multiple brand and fan accounts.
cards.use_when: A store has one video or post that clearly performed and wants more output without producing new material.

cards.title: Prioritize the Remembered Story Over the High-View Clip
cards.summary: Scroll-stopping, story-less content is forgotten the next day, while story-based creative gets remembered and converts.
cards.use_when: Deciding which of two creative concepts to scale — a high-view, low-narrative clip versus a lower-view, story-driven one.

cards.title: Break Creative Teardowns Into Micro-Elements
cards.summary: A reusable grid for diagnosing or reconstructing a video ad by isolating pacing, location, audio, text, lighting, and viewer emotion at each stage.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a poorly converting ad or briefing an editor to recreate a proven format for a store product.

cards.title: Test on a Contrarian Angle in an Unserved Audience
cards.summary: New angles reach audiences that have not been served, which is how you avoid competing for the same eyeballs as existing content.
cards.use_when: A store's ads are fatiguing or a category's messaging is saturated, and you need a new angle or audience pocket.

cards.title: Use Relatability and Proximity to Choose Story Angles
cards.summary: People remember and act on stories close to their own life situation, so match the story to where the audience actually is.
cards.use_when: Selecting which customer scenario to feature in an ad or on a landing page for a store's core buyer.

cards.title: Design Reels for Strangers, Not Followers
cards.summary: Instagram tests new Reels on non-followers first, so content must hook people who have never seen you before.
cards.use_when: Planning an organic content push for a store's Instagram and deciding what topics and hooks to lead with, or diagnosing why an existing follower base sees low reach.

cards.title: Write a Creator DNA Statement for Your Brand
cards.summary: A fill-in-the-blank positioning statement that makes brand content non-generic by default.
cards.use_when: Defining or refreshing a store's organic brand voice and positioning before planning any Reels or carousel content.

cards.title: Competitive Format Research Before Brainstorming Content
cards.summary: Mine proven high-view videos across Instagram, TikTok and YouTube by broad niche keywords, then log topics, hooks and patterns in a spreadsheet.
cards.use_when: Filling a content calendar for a store's category and needing evidence of which topics and hooks already perform instead of brainstorming from scratch.

cards.title: Find the Gap Between Proven Trends and Your Point of View
cards.summary: Turn proven competitor formats into proprietary content by filtering them through your Creator DNA to find the missing perspective.
cards.use_when: Converting researched trending formats into original store content so posts are not blind copies of competitors.

cards.title: Use Purposeful Lighting Instead of Raw Production
cards.summary: Raw and authentic does not mean bad lighting — a key light and practical background lights make hooks land harder with strangers.
cards.use_when: Setting up phone-shot video production for a store's organic content, or diagnosing why on-camera content is losing cold viewers in the first seconds.

cards.title: Write Conversational Hooks That Bypass the Ad-Blocker
cards.summary: Replace clever or alarmist hook formulas with a natural, friend-like opening line that a stranger does not recognize as marketing.
cards.use_when: Writing hook lines for Reels or short-form video that must stop cold viewers who have never seen the brand.

cards.title: Batch Content Creation in Separate Research, Writing and Filming Sessions
cards.summary: Eliminate daily overthinking by splitting research, scriptwriting and filming into distinct batched stages on different days.
cards.use_when: Building a repeatable weekly content production routine for a store's organic channel without burning out on daily posting.

cards.title: Read Macro Analytics Instead of Individual Post Flops
cards.summary: Zoom out across weeks of content to find patterns in which formats drive views, which drive followers and which drive deep engagement.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a store's organic Instagram performance to decide which formats to scale and which to stop producing.

cards.title: Attach a Comment-Triggered Lead Magnet to Reels
cards.summary: Use a ManyChat-style comment keyword automation to swap a free resource for an email address and move organic viewers onto owned lists.
cards.use_when: Setting up an organic-to-email conversion path for a store, so short-form reach feeds owned marketing channels instead of only platform followers.

cards.title: Build a Self-Feeding Content System Rather Than Chasing Virality
cards.summary: A systematic loop of stranger-focused content, batch production, macro analysis and lead capture makes growth independent of any single viral post.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to keep a store's organic content effort going long term and how to structure it so results do not depend on luck.

cards.title: Set a defensible email revenue benchmark and KPI case
cards.summary: Use the source's 30%-of-total-store-revenue benchmark to justify email investment and frame email as CAC and LTV leverage rather than a channel experiment.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much resource to put into email lifecycle, or building the internal case for hiring/agency/tooling spend.

cards.title: Complete the Klaviyo–Shopify integration and sync settings
cards.summary: Wire Shopify into Klaviyo correctly so subscriber capture, event tracking and anonymous activity all flow into one profile record.
cards.use_when: Initial account setup, a re-platform migration, or auditing why checkout/pop-up subscribers and browse events are missing from Klaviyo.

cards.title: Configure smart sending and attribution windows
cards.summary: Set the smart-sending window and choose attribution windows that match your consideration cycle, then exclude inflated data sources from reporting.
cards.use_when: Initial account configuration, or when email revenue reporting looks implausibly high/low and you need defensible numbers.

cards.title: Set brand defaults, fonts and fallbacks for email design
cards.summary: Load logo, colours, socials and custom fonts with websafe fallbacks so every email and consent page renders on-brand across inboxes.
cards.use_when: Setting up Klaviyo for the first time, or when emails render in the wrong typeface or look unbranded on some devices.

cards.title: Authenticate your domain: dedicated sending domain, SPF, DKIM, DMARC
cards.summary: Stand up a branded sending subdomain with DNS records to protect sender reputation, and keep DMARC policy at p=none to avoid self-inflicted spam filtering.
cards.use_when: New Klaviyo account, domain migration, or diagnosing poor inbox placement despite good content.

cards.title: Maintain sender reputation with bounce, spam and engagement thresholds
cards.summary: Treat sender reputation like a credit score and monitor the three inputs — bounce rate, spam complaints and engagement — against the source's thresholds.
cards.use_when: Ongoing deliverability monitoring, or when opens collapse and you need to diagnose reputation damage.

cards.title: Clean unengaged subscribers and use engagement-tiered segments
cards.summary: Suppress subscribers inactive for 180+ days and work in 14/30/60/90-day engagement windows to protect primary inbox placement.
cards.use_when: Replenishment/list hygiene work, or when deliverability declines from sending to a stale list.

cards.title: Configure preference pages and choose email opt-in deliberately
cards.summary: Match email signup confirmation and unsubscribe behavior to the store list-quality goals and applicable requirements.
cards.use_when: Account setup, when signup-to-list conversion is poor, or when unsubscribes look unbranded and abrupt.

cards.title: Map the customer journey before building flows and campaigns
cards.summary: Sequence every touchpoint — ad/organic, pop-up, welcome, campaigns, first purchase, repeat — so messages match what the subscriber already knows.
cards.use_when: Planning lifecycle architecture, or when you suspect campaigns and flows are contradicting each other.

cards.title: Use Klaviyo metrics as flow triggers and personalisation filters
cards.summary: Treat metrics (events) as the automation engine: they trigger flows and define who receives what.
cards.use_when: Building or debugging flows, especially abandoned checkout/cart, and building personalised dynamic content.

cards.title: Read a Klaviyo profile to decide segmentation and personalisation
cards.summary: Use the profile page as the single richest record of a customer — subscription source, custom properties, predictive analytics, event timeline — to drive filters and dynamic content.
cards.use_when: Designing segments, splits and conditional content, or investigating why one customer received the wrong message.

cards.title: Organise profiles into lists and segments, and never campaign to the whole list
cards.summary: Keep static lists for opt-in sources and welcome-flow triggers; use dynamic engagement-filtered segments for campaigns.
cards.use_when: Campaign sending setup, list growth tracking, or troubleshooting welcome flows sending the wrong message.

cards.title: Build the engaged prospect and engaged customer segments
cards.summary: Create engagement-qualified segments that separate first-time prospects from returning customers, then use the campaign results to learn what converts each group.
cards.use_when: Setting up your campaign sending audience, or improving deliverability and personalisation for campaigns.

cards.title: Style campaign creative by segment learning
cards.summary: Once prospect vs customer is separated, read which creative elements converted each group and repeat those elements in the channel aimed at that group.
cards.use_when: Writing campaign and welcome-series creative, or deciding what proof and offers to lead with for new vs returning buyers.

cards.title: Employ retention and account-level setup: where email sits in the 2026 lifecycle
cards.summary: Commit to a measured email cadence and a five-flow automated core, then extend with gamification, zero-party-data quizzes and split desktop/mobile experiences.
cards.use_when: Roadmapping the lifecycle programme, deciding sending frequency, and prioritising which automations to build first.

cards.title: Engagement windows as sliding retargeting filters
cards.summary: Add recent site activity to an engaged segment so returning non-openers get inbox access again, but only for a limited window.
cards.use_when: Building or auditing your campaign send segments, and deciding whether dormant subscribers should still receive campaigns.

cards.title: Build prospect and customer segments by cloning one definition
cards.summary: Create the six core segments by changing only the order-count condition and the engagement window, not by writing new definitions each time.
cards.use_when: Setting up your initial Klaviyo segment structure before launching campaigns or flows.

cards.title: Match offer intensity to engagement window
cards.summary: Send evergreen content to the most recently engaged segment and reserve big offers for the widest window.
cards.use_when: Deciding which campaign content and offers go to your 90-day versus 365-day engaged segments.

cards.title: Never send campaigns to the full list — and never to segments that are too small
cards.summary: Require an engagement filter on every campaign, but avoid slicing your sends so narrowly that you cut your monthly shots at converting a subscriber.
cards.use_when: Planning campaign send frequency and audience selection across your prospect and purchaser segments.

cards.title: Build filters so each flow only fires for the right lifecycle state
cards.summary: Profile filters are checked before every flow send, letting a welcome series stop the moment someone purchases.
cards.use_when: Setting up or debugging any automated flow where purchase or customer-type status should change who receives it.

cards.title: Micro-commitment first step in the pop-up form
cards.summary: Split the pop-up into a 'claim the offer?' step before asking for the email, then collect SMS, then show a success page.
cards.use_when: Building or redesigning your sitewide pop-up form to convert more site traffic into subscribers.

cards.title: Form behavior settings that stop accidental opt-out loss
cards.summary: Small behavior toggles — no click-outside close, immediate load, no images — prevent losing subscribers who never see the offer.
cards.use_when: Configuring display and behavior settings on a pop-up form before going live.

cards.title: Offer choice is the highest-leverage pop-up test
cards.summary: Run monthly A/B tests on the form offer first, then behavior, then copy, then design.
cards.use_when: Planning your recurring pop-up form experiment roadmap.
